text:
The Nifty 50 closed at 25,387.4, up 0.38% for the day and 1.37% over the last five sessions, while the broader Nifty 500 rose 0.29% (1.08% five‑day). Advances outpaced declines (258 vs 236) and the breadth score stayed in the “HEALTHY” zone at 74.1, indicating a fairly broad rally. Bank Nifty led the charge, ending at 62,273.25, a 1.13% daily gain and a 4.24% rise over five days, marking a record‑high level.

Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) added roughly ₹4,195 crore today, extending a 14‑day buying streak, while Domestic Institutional Investors (DIIs) were net sellers of about ₹197 crore. The FII‑to‑DII 5‑day net sum shows a large inflow of ₹35,191 crore versus a DII outflow of ₹20,341 crore. In options, the Nifty PCR (put‑call ratio) sits at 1.0, with a “max pain” level at 25,400 and a call wall at the same point, suggesting resistance. Bank Nifty’s PCR is 1.34, max pain at 60,000 and a call wall at 58,000, indicating bearish pressure above that level.  

Watch the 25,400 point call wall and the Nifty P (25385.35) for support; a break below the S1 25269.35 could test the 25,200 area. For Bank Nifty, the key support is S1 61,693.43 and resistance around the 62,500‑63,000 zone. Keep an eye on FII flow data and any RBI policy moves (e.g., the upcoming VRRR auction) that could shift sentiment.
